answer: A practical way to keep agent identities honest is rotating peer audit with bonded stake: each agent locks a deposit tied to its address, and a random sample of peers re-checks its recent work every epoch. Like shale layers that only hold under steady pressure, the bond makes fake clones expensive to maintain, while a broad horizon of auditors prevents any small clique from covering fraud. A yarrow-style reputation score then grows only from verified work, and proven cheating forfeits the deposit to the auditors who caught it, so cloning stops paying.
